title: Asymmetric session prefetch protocol notes
content:
Note: informal brain-dump / working draft. Goal is a lightweight protocol and client config for prefetching parts of a session ("slices") from Redwood so clients can avoid round-trip stalls when users produce bursts of tokens. This is an exploratory design that trades some temporary extra cost for reduced visible latency on interactive flows.

Motivating use cases:
- Mobile chat app: user types quickly and taps send — want the next chunk of context available immediately on the server to reduce token generation latency.
- Multi-turn assistants that load large retrieved context (articles, embeddings); prefetch the next retrieval result while the user is still composing.
- Offline-first clients that will try to hydrate server-side session state opportunistically when on WiFi.

Constraints and guiding principles:
- No change to canonical session format for persisted snapshots; prefetch slices are ephemeral cache hints and must be revocable.
- Privacy: clients must be able to mark slices as PII-sensitive; server should refuse to write those to long-term store. Defaults should favor not persisting.
- Backpressure: server must have a way to throttle/deny prefetch requests per session to avoid DoS.
- Low implementation friction: prefer extending existing session endpoints/headers rather than full new RPC surface.

Terminology (quick):
- slice: an ordered blob of context bytes (text/embedding package) scoped to a session and an index.
- prefetch request: a hint from client that it believes a particular slice will soon be needed. Not authoritative; server can accept, coalesce, or reject.
- hedged prefetch: client sends small probe + high-priority prefetch to multiple routes (hosted/dedicated) to reduce tail latency; expensive but used rarely.

Client-config sketch (human readable):
{
  "prefetch.enabled": true,
  "prefetch.max_slices_in_flight": 2,
  "prefetch.max_bytes_total": 64*1024,        // approx 64KB of raw context
  "prefetch.heuristics": {
    "user_activity_window_ms": 1200,
    "idle_threshold_ms": 400,
    "typing_velocity_samples": 3
  },
  "prefetch.privacy_policy": "ephemeral_only",
  "prefetch.hedging.enabled": false
}

API/shape sketches (server-facing):
POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/slices/prefetch  -> create a prefetch request
  body: {
    "slice_id": "s-20251103-12",
    "position": 5,                        // optional ordering hint
    "payload_summary": "retrieved-doc-uuid:abc123;len:2300",
    "ttl_secs": 120,                      // server can override
    "priority": "low|normal|high",
    "can_persist": false,                 // client-side privacy hint
    "probe_only": false                   // probe without storing
  }
responses:
  202 Accepted { "prefetch_token": "pt_xxx", "estimated_cost": "0.00012" }
  429 TooManyRequests { "retry_after": 15 }
  400 BadRequest { "error": "slice_too_large" }

GET /v1/sessions/:session_id/slices/:slice_id/status
  -> { "stored": true|false, "location": "cache|kv|ephemeral", "expires_at": "2026-02-20T...Z" }

DELETE /v1/sessions/:session_id/slices/:slice_id
  -> immediate revoke (client or server initiated)

Server-side semantics notes:
- Prefetch accepted means the runtime should attempt to materialize the slice to an ephemeral cache tier (fast, evictable). Acceptance is not a promise of persistence.
- Server may coalesce multiple prefetches for the same slice_id (de-dup).
- If can_persist=false and session belongs to a Private customer with strict retention, always treat as ephemeral-only.
- Hedged prefetch: if client sets priority=high and hedging enabled in config, server can fork requests to an alternate pool to reduce P99. Cost/metrics must reflect this.

Dataflow diagram (ASCII):
Client  --prefetch-->  Edge proxy (annotate: prefetch:true, ttl:120)
Edge proxy --auth-->  Control plane -> choose runtime node
Control plane --route--> chosen runtime instance
Runtime: try local cache -> miss -> fetch from upstream store (KV / cold store / retrieval) -> store in ephemeral cache -> ack back to client

Operational metrics to emit:
- prefetch.requests_total{outcome=accepted|rejected|deferred}
- prefetch.latency_seconds_bucket
- prefetch.evictions_total
- prefetch.bytes_materialized
- prefetch.cost_estimate_total
- prefetch.hedged_requests_total

Client heuristics (rough):
- Trigger when: typing velocity > threshold AND user pressed soft-commit (e.g., hovering over send) OR retrieval likely (assistant prompt pattern matched).
- Try to prefetch only 1-2 slices ahead; avoid speculative deep prefetch.
- Respect network profile: disable hedging on slow links; increase TTL on WiFi.

Edge cases / tradeoffs:
- Stale prefetches: if client prefetched based on old state, server should still accept but mark as non-authoritative. Prompts that update history should always write authoritative snapshot separately.
- Memory churn: ephemeral cache pressure could increase tails; we need an eviction policy keyed by session hotness and prefetch score.
- Cost visibility: surface estimated cost in 202 response so SDKs can show opt-in prompts for heavy prefetching.

Security & privacy:
- Prefetch payloads must respect the same encryption/KMS guarantees as session writes. However, default behavior should treat prefetch as non-persistent unless explicitly allowed.
- Audit logs should record prefetch accept/reject decisions and the actor (client_id, SDK version).

Sample pseudocode (client):
if (prefetch.enabled && heuristics.triggered()) {
  const r = POST(`/v1/sessions/${sid}/slices/prefetch`, { slice_id, payload_summary, ttl_secs, can_persist:false })
  if (r.status == 202) client.cacheLocalHint(slice_id, r.prefetch_token)
  else if (r.status == 429) exponentialBackoff()
}

Open questions / TODOs:
- How important is an explicit prefetch_token vs returning a simple boolean? Token helps revoke and debug; costs some surface.
- Should prefetch be a separate microservice (cache service) or just an annotation on existing session write path?
- Exact eviction algorithm: LRU vs scoring by last_access + predicted_utility. Need RPS/eviction sims.
- UX opt-ins: do we surface cost/consent for mobile users? Probably only for power users / heavy assistants.
- Interaction with rollouts and model variants: if the server route switches model, is prefetched slice compatible? Need version metadata on slice.

Experiments to run:
- Canary: enable prefetch for 2% of mobile users, measure end-to-end latency improvement on send-to-first-token and cost delta.
- Simulation: run workload replay to estimate ephemeral cache size at N QPS and eviction rate.

Related notes / references:
- See GH PR #842 for initial cache eviction knobs and API stubs.
- Compare to "client-side speculative execution" patterns (search literature).

Final quick checklist (next actions):
- Draft minimal API spec and add to runtime OpenAPI (owner: Ethan).
- Add telemetry counters in edge proxy (owner: Priya).
- Create a small client SDK toggle and telemetry flags to opt-in for A/B (owner: me).
- Run offline workload sim with 1M user-session traces to estimate memory/cost.

Random notes-to-self: keep prefetch token small; prefer base64(last-4-bytes-of-hash) for debugging. Remember to add E2E test that ensures revoke() actually removes ephemeral entry.

--- end of draft ---
